memo.verdict: Neutral; park, with a level. Orange Polska (OPL-PL) is a self-help cash case in a well-run Polish incumbent that the market has already paid for. At PLN 13.545 (2026-09-22) the shares trade at 12.8x consensus 24-month-forward earnings (14.0x on the record's own path) after a 57 percent rise in twelve months, the 74th percentile of their own five-year range and above the peer median of 11.7x. The 'Modal return' at a multiple settling to 12.0x is about 2.4 percent a year over eighteen months and 8.6 percent a year over three years against the framework's 20 percent bar, an F. The return fails the bar at every multiple up to today's 14.0x held, on the record's earnings and on consensus. Direction neutral because the business is sound and the price is full; park because the return fails and because the 'Target Setup' that fits ('Major Corporate Change') is at its endpoint. The gate does not park the case: no D or F sits on management (C), business quality (C), predictability (B) or trackability (C); the return does. Conviction medium. The level at which the record would progress the case: about PLN 10.5 to PLN 11 (about 11x 24-month-forward on the record's earnings, about 10x on consensus), where the modal return clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months and the dividend yield is near 6 percent. The likeliest route to that level is a Q3 2026 print on 26 October 2026 with IT and integration revenue below PLN 400 million or indirect costs rising, which would not by itself break the case. Ten ratings in the record; none moved from the analysis notes' provisional ratings.
case: The thesis: Orange Polska is a self-help cash case in a well-run Polish incumbent, and it is a good case that the market has already paid for; the change is real, broad and fully propagated, and its materiality to a return from this price is what fails.

The change is internal, broad and three years into its course. Six of twelve screened internal forces are strong: guidance raised twice in 2026 and on every line (A); standards and cost discipline measurably improved, with underlying indirect costs flat in 1H 2026 against a 5.5 percent contractual wage rise and 384 of 540 planned 2026 departures done by June (B); real, repeated price rises, a PLN 5 rise across core consumer services in Q1 2026, 3.6 percent CPI indexation, automatic PLN 5 to PLN 10 post-loyalty steps, convergent ARPO +4.5 percent (B); shareholder returns stepped up every year from PLN 0.25 (2022) to PLN 0.61 with a floor through 2028 (B); wholesale fibre monetisation with third-party lines +41 percent (B); perimeter simplified, Orange Energia sold, copper sales ceased, subsidiaries merged (B). Absent are the pattern's sharpest markers: no chief executive change (D), no other leadership change (D), no balance-sheet use at 1.0x against a 1.7x to 2.2x corridor (D). None of the screen's red flags is present.

The external forces are mild tailwinds, not a demand inflection (C). Competition easing (B): all four operators raised tariffs under more-for-more formulas, Play the net donor in portability, the industry moved from overbuild to open-access sharing; against it T-Mobile's single PLN 75 a month unlimited plan. Regulation a tailwind (B): the telecoms regulator lifted bitstream and local-loop obligations on 20 January 2026 after twenty years; against it a PLN 34 million consumer-protection fine, open investigations into indexation clauses, and P4's PLN 630 million damages claim (about 63 percent of a year's organic cash flow). Supply side a tailwind (B): electricity contracted to 2035 at about PLN 459 per MWh, maintenance -3 percent; labour the headwind at 5.5 percent and at least 5 percent contractual rises. Demand steady (C): core telecom +4.9 percent, down from 6.5 percent in 2025; Polish fixed broadband and mobile prices 49 and 86 percent below EU averages, a price runway not a demand swing. The parent a standing headwind of about 6 percent of EBITDAaL a year (C).
counter_case: At its strongest, at 'Investment Thesis': the market is right to pay 12.8x and is still under-paying. A telecom operator with a 1.0x balance sheet, 100 percent local-currency debt, a dividend floor covering two-thirds of guided cash and growing 15 percent a year, an oligopoly that indexes prices, a footprint reaching two-thirds of Polish homes at 13 percent capital intensity, flat depreciation for three years and a management that has beaten every annual target since 2021 is a compounder in a sector of ex-growth incumbents. The twelve-month re-rating is the market catching up with a business that changed between 2021 and 2025, not overshooting it; the multiple deserves the Nordic and Swiss quality names' 14x to 20x, not the incumbents' 12x. Consensus at PLN 1.08 for FY2028 is if anything low, because the sell-side has booked 2H 2026 as a revenue decline; the June to September fall of 18 percent is profit-taking after a 100 percent rise, not a verdict. At 14x consensus 24-month-forward earnings of PLN 1.19 in March 2028 the shares are worth PLN 16.7 plus PLN 0.72 of dividend, a return of 28 percent over eighteen months, 18 percent a year: a C nearly a B. Every operating fact in this argument is in the record; the twelve-month return was company-driven; the quality names in the set trade at 14x to 20x on lower growth.

The record concedes the delivery, the balance sheet, the dividend's sustainability, the oligopoly's discipline, that the sell-side's FY2026 revenue line looks too low, that the framework's mediocrity calibration reads a defensive telecom's natural Cs as weakness, and that for a yield investor this is a sound hold.
triggers: - The progress level: about PLN 10.5 to PLN 11 (about 11x 24-month-forward on the record's earnings, about 10x on consensus; a dividend yield near 6 percent), where the modal return clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months; on the adverse drop-through path the level falls to about PLN 9.2.

- Q3 2026 results, 26 October 2026: IT and integration revenue above PLN 450 million confirms, below PLN 450 million is the alarm, below PLN 400 million is the invalidate level for the business-IT line and the counter-thesis level; EBITDAaL margin excluding one-offs above 26.5 percent confirms; a print below PLN 400 million or with indirect costs rising is the likeliest route to the progress level and would not by itself break the case.
- Indirect costs: confirm flat or down; alarm up more than 1 percent in 2H 2026; invalidate above +2 percent for the year.

- Convergent ARPO growth: confirm above 4 percent; alarm below 4 percent; invalidate below 3.5 percent for two quarters. Postpaid handset ARPO growth: alarm below 1.0 percent; invalidate negative for two quarters.
- Core telecom service growth: alarm below 4 percent; invalidate below 3 percent for two quarters.

- Wholesale fibre line net additions: confirm above 15 thousand a quarter. FiberCo take-up: confirm 35 percent by Q2 2027; invalidate below 32 percent. Retail fibre net additions: alarm below 20 thousand a quarter; invalidate below 15 thousand a quarter (the false-friend test, read against wholesale additions on the same footprint).
